title: Bet Track Building and Reading Words

lessons.title: Blend ahhh and eee
lessons.goal: Blend a familiar consonant and vowel without guessing a whole word.
new: Bet says b; Vet says v.
teach: The stick and the stick with a handle say ahhh in these examples. The pea beneath says eee.
Find the letter, look beneath, then join the sounds: m plus ahhh makes mah; m plus eee makes mee.
A dot inside Mem keeps its m sound. A final Aleph is quiet in our two family words.
steps: Read each small sound before blending the whole word.
Point to the mother and father in the picture. Read their labels.
Say each word again without using the picture to guess.

questions.why: The pea beneath Mem gives eee: mee.

tasks: Copy father and circle its ahhh marks
lessons.check: I can blend ahhh and eee and read two family words.
answers: Read mah, mee, bah, bee, vee.
Copy father, ah-ba; circle both ahhh marks.
lessons.alt: A mother, father, and child together

lessons.title: Close a word with a consonant
lessons.goal: Read the final consonant without adding an extra vowel.
new: Yud says y at the start of these words.
Mem changes to ם at the end; it still says m.
teach: Read a letter and its vowel, then close with the last consonant. Do not add ahhh after the final letter.
Yud with the ahhh handle, followed by final Mem, makes yam: sea. Yud plus ahhh and Dalet makes yad: hand.
Yud can also help write the eee sound after another letter. In מִי, the whole word says mee, meaning who.
steps: Blend the vowel, then finish with m or d.
Use the sea and hand picture to check meaning after reading.

questions.why: Sea is יָם, yam. The final Mem closes the word.

options: With d, without an added vowel
questions.why: The last letter is Dalet with no vowel beneath it here. Finish with d.

tasks: Copy sea and underline its final Mem
lessons.check: I can close yam and yad without adding a vowel.
answers: Read yam and yad without an extra final vowel.
Copy sea, yam; underline final Mem.
lessons.alt: Sea waves and an open hand

lessons.title: Read the over vowel oh
lessons.goal: Recognize both common oh spellings and blend a word for light.
new: Resh says r; follow your teacher.
Vav with the dot over says oh here.
teach: The over vowel says ohhhver oh. Look above the letter.
Oh may be written as a dot over a letter or with Vav carrying the dot above. Both patterns below say moh.
Vav is helping write a vowel in וֹ. Do not add a v sound.
steps: Find the dot above in each model.
Blend oh and r. Finish with r, without an added vowel.
Read the word, then point to the light in the picture.

questions.prompt: What does Vav contribute in וֹ?
questions.why: In this pattern Vav carries oh. Do not add v.

tasks: Copy light and circle its over dot
lessons.check: I can recognize oh and read or for light.
answers: Copy light; circle the dot above Vav.
lessons.alt: Sunlight shining through an open window

lessons.title: Read the belly vowel oo
lessons.goal: Read both oo patterns and decode two pictured words.
new: Tav says t. A dot inside does not change its t sound.
Vav with a dot in its belly says oo.
teach: A dot touching Vav at its belly gives oo, as in moon. Say oo without adding v.
Three descending dots beneath a letter also give oo. The two Mem models below both say moo.
Keep oo smooth between the first and last consonants: s-oo-s and t-oo-t.
steps: Find the belly dot and the three-dot staircase.
Read the word before using the picture.
Point to the horse or a strawberry to show meaning.

questions.why: The three-dot staircase and belly Vav both give oo.

tasks: Copy horse and circle the belly dot
lessons.check: I can read oo without adding v, then say the word meaning.
answers: Copy horse, soos; circle the belly dot.
lessons.alt: A standing horse and three strawberries

lessons.title: Read eh and ay carefully
lessons.goal: Distinguish the three eggs from the two side-by-side dots.
new: Chet says kh, a throat sound as in Bach.
Nun says n; final ן keeps the n sound.
teach: Three eggs beneath the letter give eh, as in eggs. The two side-by-side dots use our class cue ay, as in brake.
Many modern Hebrew speakers pronounce both signs as eh. Follow one teacher model consistently; do not mark a familiar community pronunciation wrong.
Use final Mem and final Nun to close the words. Pictures check meaning; the marks tell you how to read.
steps: Point to each vowel and say eh or the class ay cue.
Read bread slowly, joining the last m without adding a vowel.
Read son with your teacher: class bayn; often ben in modern Hebrew.

questions.why: אֶ has three dots. Our cue is eh as in eggs.

tasks: Read and compare the vowel marks
Copy son and underline final Nun
lessons.check: I can distinguish the marks and read bread and son with my teacher.
answers: Class cues: leh and lay. Accept the teacher model.
Copy son; underline final Nun. Class bayn or modern ben.
lessons.alt: A loaf of bread with two slices on a plate

lessons.title: Read a greeting with meaning
lessons.goal: Blend known patterns into shalom and two short greetings.
new: Shin has its dot on the right and says sh.
Final Mem closes with m, without an extra vowel.
teach: Find the right-hand dot on Shin. This dot gives sh; the mark beneath supplies the vowel.
Blend sh plus ahhh, then l plus oh, then close with m: sha-lom.
Shalom can mean peace and is also used as hello or goodbye. Use the greeting scene to act out hello.
steps: Read shalom without a picture hint.
Read each greeting, then tell whom you greeted.
Act out one greeting with a study partner.

questions.why: אִמָּא means mother, so שָׁלוֹם אִמָּא says hello, Mom.

options: With m, without an extra vowel
questions.why: Final Mem closes the word with m.

tasks: Copy hello, Dad, then explain it
lessons.check: I can read and explain two short greetings without guessing.
answers: Read hello, Dad and hello, Mom.
Copy hello, Dad; accept goodbye, Dad in matching context.
lessons.alt: Two children waving hello on a path
